Every shape in the roster asks what the source DOES — a drift silhouette,
a judged row, a verb glyph. `default-param` asks something else: whether
a form SYNTAX declares is written here at all.

That is the question an oracle-blind probe opens with, since the board is
green on what the wheel does and silent on everything else, and until now
it could only be answered from outside the medium. Establishing that the
wheel writes no default-valued parameter took two greps behind two
mentl-skip confessions the day before, one for the count and one to prove
the file set non-empty so the zero was a verdict.

The detector reads the carrier the graph already holds: a default is
TParam slot 4, an Option(Node) the parser fills at the declaration, so
the count is a chase to a proven fact rather than a re-derivation from
source text. No new graph state, no writer added, and the walk was
already O(nodes).

The medium now answers `0 default-valued parameter(s)` about its own
weave, confirming the grep's verdict through a different channel.

failed against the standing boot, then passed against the new pin. The
fixture line was read back from the artifact rather than counted.

Siblings stay separate arms on purpose — labeled arguments, as-patterns,
record rest, named row aliases each read their own carrier, so each is
one more variant rather than a generalized surface parameter.

mentl/fe5b2c0:
The page's stub shim could not run the live boot (a spawning module:
shared-image import + wasi.thread-spawn, a thread per judged stmt), so
the IDE had pinned a pre-spawn wheel and called the skew a boundary.
The blocker is now designed instead of described: ide/wheel-worker.js
is the one execution host — the page and the node twin drive the same
file — and ide/mentl-ide.wasm re-derives from the live boot with the
memory import's declared min shrunk 65536 -> 8192 pages.

Two browser host facts forced the shape, both measured against node,
which has neither (the identical blob ran there 3.5s/252 tasks against
a 90s Chrome hang): the join's memory.atomic.wait32 is forbidden on
the main thread, so the page never instantiates the module; and Chrome
flushes a worker's outgoing postMessages only when the sender yields,
which thread-spawn never does — it fires mid-wasm and the root then
blocks in the join (probed: 16 spawns logged, zero task starts, pool
provably loaded). Dispatch therefore rides a SharedArrayBuffer ring +
Atomics.notify into a pool of workers armed before _start can block;
completion stays on the wheel's own task-record protocol, so the
message channel can never fabricate a result. The pool also cut node's
blob compile 3.5s -> 0.97s (252 worker boots -> 12).

tools/ide-gate.sh holds it green: the node twin's four faces (the
stub-spawn RED control traps unreachable against this wasm — the
measured reason for the old pin), then headless chrome reads the
served page's ?smoke console wire: exit=0 tasks=252 watlines=4403
ms=932, wat line-count identical to node.

two-top/fe6ce08:
Once matchbox's signaling loop dies (server unreachable after its
built-in retries), update_peers unwraps the closed channel and aborts
the process — a phone with no network crashed about six seconds after
tapping FIND OPPONENT. Poll with try_update_peers and treat a dead
socket as a refusal: drop the driver, park the lobby at Idle, and
leave QUIT and PLAY THE BOT one tap away. The SUMMONING overlay's
stall diagnosis already names the likely cause during the wait.
two-top/fed7008:
TURN credentials must never ship inside a distributed binary (one
strings invocation extracts them), so the relay path moves to the TURN
REST API convention: crates/ice_vendor is a runtime-free HTTP service
that holds the secret server-side and answers GET /ice with a throwaway
pair the TURN server refuses once the timestamp in the username expires.
Two backends by env: coturn use-auth-secret HMAC (verified live against
an independent python HMAC-SHA1), or a proxy over Cloudflare's TURN
credential generator so the only secret anywhere is the API token the
vendor holds. Neither configured answers STUN-only, which still
exercises the whole client path.

Client side, netplay.rs: when TWOTOP_ICE_URL is set (a URL, never a
credential — safe to bake into public builds), match entry kicks the
fetch on the IO task pool and finish_ice_fetch opens the socket with
whatever arrives, falling back to the baked/STUN-only config after
2.5 s so a dead vendor costs seconds, not the match. The fetch rides
the SUMMONING wait; a quit during a pending fetch can no longer open a
socket after leaving the screen. The TWOTOP_TURN_* bake survives as
the local-testing path only.

The APK workflow bakes the vendor URL from a repo variable; the
determinism matrix excludes the server crate from cross-target builds
(it never runs on a phone); SIGNALING.md documents both backends and
the deploy path.
